Tenant thread with property manager

Tenant, 6:02pm: Hey, small thing — the smoke detector in the hallway has been chirping every 30 seconds or so, probably just needs a new battery. Not urgent, whenever you get a chance.
Manager, 6:10pm: Thanks for the heads up, I'll put in a work order for this week.
Tenant, 6:15pm: Sounds good, no rush at all, it's just a little annoying background noise.
Manager, 6:16pm: Totally understand, we'll get a fresh battery in there in the next few days.
Tenant, 7:45pm: Update — sorry, this is a bit more concerning now. I can actually smell something like burning plastic near that same hallway detector, and it just started beeping continuously instead of chirping. I don't see smoke or flame yet but the smell is getting stronger.
Manager, 7:47pm: That's a different situation — please evacuate the unit now and call 911 or the fire department non-emergency line, don't wait for maintenance for this. I'm calling our emergency electrician too in case it's a wiring issue in the wall behind that detector.
Tenant, 7:50pm: Ok, stepping outside now with my dog, will update you.
Manager, 7:52pm: Good, stay outside until the fire department or electrician clears the unit. I've also notified the two adjacent units on that hallway as a precaution, since the wiring could run through a shared wall.
Tenant, 8:20pm: Fire department checked it out, said it looks like an old wiring junction overheating behind the detector, not an active fire, but they cut power to that circuit until an electrician can inspect it properly tomorrow. Smell is gone now that the circuit's off.
Manager, 8:25pm: Great, thank you for evacuating so quickly and for the detailed updates throughout, that genuinely made this easier to handle well. I've scheduled the electrician for 8am tomorrow and blocked that hallway outlet circuit in our system so nobody accidentally re-energizes it overnight.
Tenant, 8:26pm: No power in the hallway means no hallway lights though, is that safe overnight?
Manager, 8:28pm: Good catch — the emergency battery-backed hallway lighting is on a separate circuit so that part is unaffected, you'll still have emergency lighting, just not the regular ceiling fixtures. I'll also swap the smoke detector itself for a new unit tomorrow morning as a precaution even though the wiring, not the detector, seems to be the root cause.
Tenant, 8:35pm: That all makes sense, thank you for taking this seriously and moving so fast. Heading back inside now that the smell's cleared and the fire department gave the ok.
